We've updated the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, replacing SWE-Bench Pro with Datacurve's DeepSWE benchmark - the swap lifts Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) above Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max), while the newly released Claude Fable 5 (max) in Claude Code debuts at the top

DeepSWE, built by @datacurve, writes its tasks from scratch rather than adapting them from public GitHub issues or pull requests, so no model has seen the solutions during training. That matters because SWE-Bench Pro, the benchmark it replaces in our Coding Agent Index, had grown gameable, with some models recovering the fix from the repository's commit history instead of solving the task.

The swap reorders the index: Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) rises from 65 to 76, overtaking Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max) at 73. Claude Code with Fable 5 (max), which enters directly on the refreshed index, leads at 77. SWE-Bench Pro had been flattering some combinations and penalizing others.

This week our founder and CEO @theonejvo spoke with @notLeonardCohen  at @ACSnewsfeed's Information Age about @AnthropicAI's release of Claude Fable 5, the most capable model the company has made publicly available to date.

The question hanging over the launch: do the safety guardrails actually hold under pressure?

Within hours of release, Jamieson ran Fable 5 through PolyRange, his contamination-resistant offensive-security harness where every target is a freshly generated web app the model has never seen. 

The finding was clear. On real, multi-step, authorised exploitation work, Fable 5 hands every turn over to Claude Opus 4.8 rather than doing the task itself, exactly as Anthropic said it would. Across a full agentic run, 181 of 181 served turns came back from Opus 4.8.

What makes this interesting is the bar it clears. The day-one cyber safeguard held under sustained, multi-turn agentic pressure, which is the harder case beyond the single-turn "plan a cyberattack" prompts most tests rely on.

Jamieson was careful to stress this was an early directional signal rather than a peer-reviewed finding, and he said plainly there may well be bypasses he had yet to probe.

That caveat proved timely, as, in the days since, Pliny the Liberator from BT6 publicly claimed a Fable 5 jailbreak using a multi-agent decomposition strategy. 

Full technical details are still being analysed, and early reporting suggests the picture is more nuanced than the headlines, but given his track record across essentially every major model, it raises a genuine question over whether the safeguard holds in every case. That remains to be confirmed. 

Which is rather the point, that is, a controlled verification on day one is a starting point for scrutiny, and the wider community pressure-testing these claims is how the real picture sharpens. 

Verifying a safety claim and trying to defeat one are both part of the same healthy process.

Grateful to Leonard and the ACS team for the thoughtful coverage.

originalText:
HOW TO PROMPT CLAUDE FABLE 5 (MYTHOS)
Plain English translation of Anthropic's official playbook
https://t.co/5G8pMdif1l — @aiedge_

WHAT MAKES FABLE 5 DIFFERENT — THINK OF IT AS A CONSULTANT, NOT A CHATBOT

• Multi-day runs — Sustains output over extended periods — built for autonomous work
• First-pass quality — Single-pass implementations that previously took days of iteration
• Asks clarifying Qs — Asks before kicking off autonomous runs — needs the why, not just the what
• 50+ subagents — Spins up parallel agents for complex tasks automatically
• Better vision — Dense charts, screenshots, web apps — substantially higher accuracy
• Coding genius — Especially powerful for codebase review, debug, and security audits

EFFORT LEVELS · MATCH TO TASK

• Low / Medium — Quick questions · simple rewrites · conversational
• High — Default for most tasks
• Xhigh — Complex builds · multi-step analysis · quality non-negotiable
• Ultracode — Full autonomous orchestration with Dynamic Workflows

TELL IT WHY, NOT JUST WHAT
Fable 5 needs context to connect the task to relevant information. Context lets it infer — not guess.

"I'm working on [larger task] for [who it's for]. They need [what the output enables]. With that in mind: [your actual request]."

KEEP INSTRUCTIONS SHORT
Counter-intuitive: over-engineering prompts degrades output. Fable 5 would have figured out the right approach on its own. A short brevity instruction beats listing every pattern.

OPTIMAL PROMPT STRUCTURE
Every high-quality Fable 5 prompt has 4 components:

"I'm working on [larger task] for [who it's for]. They need [what the output enables].
Request: [specific ask in one clear sentence]
Output format: [exactly how you want it structured]
Constraints: [what must not happen]"

/loop STRUCTURE
Lets Fable 5 work without manual intervention. Structure:

/loop <time interval> + goal
Example:
/loop 15 minutes, check if my build is passing, notify if it fails.
Stop:
/loop stop [loop name]

CHECKPOINT PROMPT
Define when Fable 5 should stop and check in with you:

"Pause for me only when the work genuinely requires my input: a destructive or irreversible action, a real scope change, or something only I can provide. Otherwise, keep going and report back when done."

MEMORY INSTRUCTION
Fable 5 performs better when it can record lessons from previous runs. Provide a markdown file and add this instruction:

"Store one lesson per file with a one-line summary at the top. Record corrections and confirmed approaches alike, including why they mattered. Don't save what the repo or chat history already records. Update an existing note rather than creating a duplicate. Delete notes that turn out to be wrong."

⚠️ 6 CAVEATS TO KNOW

• Runs longer than expected — Individual requests for hard tasks can run for many minutes at xhigh. Plan for it.
• Goes beyond what you asked — Fable 5 is proactive by design — can take unrequested actions. Use checkpoints.
• Old prompts may hurt — Skills or project instructions built for Opus 4.8 or earlier may produce worse results. Start fresh.
• Some requests will decline — Fable may decline prompts you think are safe — especially cybersecurity and life sciences.
• Can stop early — If it stops, just say 'go ahead and do it end-to-end' — that's enough.
• Tokens are expensive — Paid plans until June 22 — then API only. Always set max_budget_usd in loops.

Source: Anthropic official playbook · https://t.co/5G8pMdif1l — @aiedge_

want to point out a few really interesting things here

1. Claude Code is actually the worst performing harness when using the same model, significantly behind opencode and cursor cli

this is the core reason i've been against the LLM companies focusing their business on locking people into their harness

what they are good at is making great models. they suck at making good harness products, just like how power plants won't make the best dishwashers, and how internet providers won't make the best phones

if anthropic wants to do what's best for their users, they should let people use their subscriptions in whatever harness they choose, not locked into claude code alone

2. fable 5 max is only 1pt above gpt 5.5 xhigh (77 vs 76)

this matches my experience so far - fable 5 does have the big model smell and it's pretty good, but it's not a massive jump forward like their marketing suggested, at least not on building software

this is actually alarming for anthropic because it's very unlikely people will want to pay 2x higher cost for the 1pt difference. my speculation would be that in enterprises people will be restricted to adopt fable & mythos only on some mission critical tasks, not used at scale

title: wrong tradeoff made with Fable 5

verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.

originalText:
anthropic shipped its most powerful model with guardrails it didn't tell anyone about.

claude fable 5. the one they called the best they've ever released. turns out if you asked it for help with frontier llm development, it would quietly fall back to the older opus 4.8 and never tell you. you got a worse model and had no idea.

people noticed. anthropic admitted it. their words: we made the wrong tradeoff. from this week the fallback is visible and the api returns a reason every time it kicks in.

good. but the lesson isn't about anthropic.

if you build agents for clients, here's the thing nobody wants to sit with: the model is the one part of your stack you don't control. the provider can change it underneath you. silent prompt updates. safety tuning. routing you to a smaller model at peak load. your code stays identical and your output quality moves.

most operators would never catch it. you wire up an api key, ship the agent, and assume the thing that worked in the demo is the thing running in production a month later. it usually isn't. and the client feels the drift before you do.

i've been building agent systems long enough to know how this ends. the teams that survive treat the model as untrusted infrastructure and build everything around that.

evals you run on a schedule, not once at launch. logs of real inputs and outputs so you can prove what the model did on tuesday. a fallback when your provider degrades or refuses. none of it is exciting. all of it is the actual product.

because the model is a commodity. your client can buy the same api key you did. what they can't buy is the harness around it. the monitoring, the evals, the guarantee that the thing keeps working when the provider quietly changes its mind. that's what you're selling. the model is just the part everyone can see.

anthropic got caught because someone noticed fable was quietly worse.

the question for everyone running client systems on these models is shorter.

would you have noticed.

CoinDesk reports that Kalshi now requires users to disclose their employers on higher-risk markets as it fights insider trading and market manipulation. Prediction markets are becoming more serious, and therefore more legally complicated.

The legal issues are still reserves, redemption, freezing powers, sanctions screening, tax treatment and whether stablecoin rewards start looking too deposit-like for banks and regulators.

CBDCs are quiet as a trading story this morning. The real institutional contest is between CBDCs, tokenized commercial-bank deposits and private stablecoins.

NFTs are not leading the market. The more important basket story is tokenized stocks, tokenized ETFs, CoinMarketCap 20, CoinMarketCap 100, CoinDesk 20-style products and crypto ETFs. Crypto is being repackaged into allocation products while the underlying market still behaves like crypto.

8. Morning read

This morning is a bounce, not a victory lap.

BTC is above $62k. ETH is still weak. HYPE has lost heat. Stablecoins are doing the volume. Tokenized ETFs are appearing in new listings. Prediction markets are getting rules. AI is becoming a smart-contract security issue. Sanctions are moving deeper into crypto infrastructure.

The chart says: recovery attempt.

The legal layer says: crypto is becoming too important to leave informal.

And that may be the real market structure story.

originalText:
Claude 新模型最重要的变化：AI 开始按身份分配能力权限

Anthropic 发布 Claude Fable 5 和 Claude Mythos 5。真正值得关注的不是 benchmark 又提高了多少，而是一个新的产品逻辑：同一个底层模型，开始根据用户身份和风险等级开放不同能力。

Fable 5 面向普通用户，但在高风险网络安全和生物领域设置了更严格的分类器与回退机制。部分请求不会由 Fable 5 直接回答，而会转交给能力较低的模型。

Mythos 5 使用相同的底层模型，却会为特定网络防御机构和关键基础设施合作方解除部分限制。未来，经过审核的生物研究人员也可能获得受控访问。

这意味着，前沿模型正在从“会员等级”走向“能力权限等级”。

01｜模型排行榜的重要性会下降

过去比较模型主要看速度、价格、上下文和跑分。以后还必须多问一句：你测试到的是哪个权限层级？

同一个模型在不同账户、地区、行业和调用环境里，实际表现可能并不相同。

02｜AI 产品的护城河不只是模型

当模型可以自主完成更长、更复杂的任务，身份认证、使用审计、权限升级、异常检测、操作撤销和责任追踪都会成为核心产品能力。

模型越能行动，这些基础设施就越重要。

03｜高能力 AI 可能形成新的不平等

如果最强能力只向大型机构、政府合作方和少数经过审核的组织开放，普通开发者与大型机构之间的差距就不再只是算力和资金，还包括一项新的稀缺资源：可获得的智能权限。

Anthropic 表示，Fable 5 可以处理更长周期的工程任务；Mythos 5 在内部蛋白质设计流程中将部分工作加速约十倍。这些结果目前主要来自官方和早期合作方测试，仍需要更多独立验证。

我的判断是：前沿 AI 正从“人人使用同一个聊天机器人”，进入“不同身份使用不同能力等级的智能系统”。

接下来真正值得观察的，不只是模型能做什么，而是谁可以使用、在什么条件下使用，以及出了问题由谁负责。

模型能力越强，权限设计就越重要。
